The widening of the 90% confidence intervals as the time horizon extends directly reflects the increasing uncertainty inherent in longer-term predictions. While these intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain high-impact events could still push the actual value outside the forecasted boundaries. Additionally, events specific to the underlying asset, such as a major regulatory change, a significant technological disruption, or a company-specific scandal, could also lead to extreme deviations not fully captured within standard probabilistic models.
